findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns error IDs with event data when nodestore returns partial results
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict that may omit missing node_ids. The subsequent zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes a 1:1 positional correspondence between the error_ids list and the dict values. If any event is missing from nodestore, the dict will have fewer entries than error_ids, causing all subsequent error_ids to be paired with the wrong event data. This produces ErrorEvent objects with mismatched id/title/message, corrupting the AI summary input. The fix is to iterate over zip(node_ids, error_ids) and look up each node_id in the events dict individually.

findings.title: Static method references PRCommentWorkflow which may not be in scope in commit_context.py
findings.body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration and calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title). However, _truncate_title is defined as a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration itself in this same class. If PRCommentWorkflow is not defined or imported in this module (it appears to be defined in or imported by the GitHub/GitLab integration modules), this will raise a NameError at runtime when any PR comment is generated. The call should be CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title) to reference the method on the class where it is actually defined.

findings.title: Mutual exclusion validation between age and timestamp uses truthiness, missing zero-valued fields
findings.body: validate_timestamp checks 'if self.initial_data.get("age")' and validate_age checks 'if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")'. These are truthiness checks, so if a browser sends age=0 alongside timestamp (or timestamp=0 alongside age), the validation will not detect the conflict and will accept the report as valid. The spec requires these fields to be mutually exclusive. The check should use 'is not None' or '"age" in self.initial_data' to correctly detect presence regardless of value.

findings.title: get_request_data mutates its input list via in-place sort
findings.body: get_request_data calls error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) which sorts the list in place. The caller (analyze_recording_segments) passes the error_events list received from the endpoint. While the list is not reused after this call in the current code path, mutating a function argument is a hidden side effect that can cause subtle bugs if the caller's expectations change. Using sorted(error_events, key=...) would avoid the mutation.

findings.title: Timestamp unit mismatch between error events and replay segment events may cause incorrect interleaving
findings.body: gen_request_data compares error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] with event.get("timestamp", 0) to interleave errors chronologically. Error event timestamps from nodestore are Unix epoch seconds (float). Replay segment event timestamps may be in seconds or milliseconds depending on the SDK version and platform. If the units differ, all errors will be sorted before or after all breadcrumb events, producing a nonsensical timeline for the AI summary. The code should normalize both timestamp sources to the same unit before comparison.

findings.title: analytics.record accesses request.user.id unconditionally which may fail for non-user auth
findings.body: The analytics.record call passes user_id=request.user.id. While the endpoint requires ProjectReleasePermission, if the request is authenticated via an org auth token (as suggested by the is_org_auth_token_auth check later in the method), request.user may not be a standard User object with an id attribute. The analytics event defines user_id as required=False, so passing None or omitting it would be safer than assuming request.user.id always exists.
